A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation and translation experiments on AFHQ, CelebA-HQ and CelebA, including quantitative comparisons and sparsity/dimensionality analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds colored/rotated MNIST experiments, an alternative sparsity-penalty experiment and additional training-time results.

M1.justification: Appendix H.4 adds an implemented sparsity-penalty variant using p = 1/2 instead of the previously evaluated ℓ1 penalty. The underlying LDM constraints, coupled GAN formulation and GAN-inversion translation procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix H.1 adds a controlled MNIST generation benchmark with colored and rotated domains, treating digit identity as content. This extends coverage beyond natural faces while retaining the existing image-task family and all three earlier datasets.

E2.justification: The corresponding generation comparisons retain I-GAN, StyleGAN-ADA and Transitional-cGAN; translation retains StarGANv2, SmoothGAN and the I-GAN variants. The new appendix experiments introduce no additional external baseline.

E3.justification: The added MNIST protocol uses 60,000 training images per domain, 32×32 resolution, smaller networks, Adam at 0.0001, batch size 128 and 500 epochs, with λ = 0.15 versus 0. Existing natural-image splits, training budgets and FID/LPIPS procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix H.1 extends the existing sparsity-removal diagnostic to digit identity, color and rotation. H.4 adds a check of an alternative sparsity penalty, and G.7 reports qualitative sensitivity observations involving initialization, hyperparameters and encoder depth. The earlier underestimated-dimension analysis is retained as H.6.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same style-diversity standard deviations. v3 adds no explicit seed identities, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests; G.7's initialization-sensitivity discussion does not specify a statistical estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds generation runtimes. New MNIST results report average FID 22.08 with sparsity versus 24.08 without it, and the p = 1/2 AFHQ variant reports FID 6.61. These are additional results under specified settings; earlier FID, diversity and dimensionality-ablation values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 corrects the pushforward definition's measurable set from the source space X to the target space Y. A.2 adds a property concerning enlargement of a function's codomain. Appendix E expands manifold/Jacobian explanations, while the principal theorem statements and core proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and concluding claims retain the same scope: relaxed identifiability conditions, sparsity-based identification without exact latent dimensions, and an equivalent GAN implementation. The new experiments support these existing contributions.

C2.justification: Section 7 newly identifies continuous-data applicability and GAN training instability as limitations, explaining that discrete modalities require extensions. Appendix G.7 additionally identifies encoders deeper than five layers as a convergence risk. Earlier limitations concerning homogeneous domains and underestimated dimensions remain.

D1.justification: v3 documents MNIST rotation/color preprocessing, layer-by-layer architectures in Tables 3–4, optimizer settings and training duration. It also expands runtime reporting. Existing natural-image implementation details and baseline-code access links are retained.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds application references to Hong et al. (2024), Huang et al. (2022) and Dai et al. (2023); Appendix E adds a differential-geometry reference. The central positioning against earlier identifiability work and I-GAN remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The established narrative is largely retained, with localized explanatory additions, explicit proof pointers, Remark 4.1, additional appendix subsections and acknowledgments. The guided-translation discussion moves into Appendix H.2, and conference-header text is added.

P2.justification: The experimental displays expand substantially through new MNIST and alternative-penalty figures and two architecture tables. Table 1 gains training-time columns. The original Figure 4 is split between v3 Figure 4 and appendix Figure 8, with further resizing and relocation of retained figures; no earlier image panels are lost.

improvement.justification: The controlled MNIST examples make content leakage without sparsity easier to assess, while the alternative-penalty experiment provides additional support for the regularization approach. Added implementation details, runtime comparisons and explicit applicability/stability limitations improve transparency. These are useful incremental gains: the central theoretical results and existing benchmark findings remain essentially unchanged, and the additional experiments provide no new repeated-run uncertainty estimates.
